unit.title: Put the clock behind a seam
A fake store that keeps the database's rules

fund-csharp/21-testing-web-apps-seams-an.instructions:
**Skills:** TimeProvider · seams · boundary instants  
**Level:** ★★☆

**Interview prompt.** "Invites expire 7 days after they are created. The code calls `DateTimeOffset.UtcNow` twice and its tests assert 'about a week'. Make it testable to the exact instant."

**Why it matters.** `TimeProvider` is the clock seam of the base library: production passes `TimeProvider.System`, a test passes a clock it controls (test factories swap it in `ConfigureTestServices`). Reading the clock once per operation keeps every timestamp of one action on the same instant.

**Your task.**
- Complete `ManualClock` in the types section: a `TimeProvider` whose `GetUtcNow()` returns the instant it was created with; `Advance(TimeSpan by)` moves it forward, and advances add up. A negative `by` throws `ArgumentOutOfRangeException` (this clock never runs backwards).
- `Invite Create(TimeProvider clock, string email)`: `CreatedAt` is now and `ExpiresAt` is exactly 7 days later. Read the clock ONCE.
- `int Accept(TimeProvider clock, Invite invite)`: 200 while now is before `ExpiresAt`, 410 (Gone) from `ExpiresAt` on.

Use only the `clock` you are given. The tests also use a `TickingClock` (types section) that moves 1 ms forward on every read, to catch a second read.

**Worked example.** A clock at 1 March 09:00 creates an invite expiring 8 March 09:00; at 8 March 08:59:59 `Accept` gives 200, at 09:00:00 it gives 410.
hints: A test can only pin what the code takes as input, so the time must come from the clock parameter.

Keep the current instant in a field of the fake and move it in Advance after refusing a negative step. In Create take the time once and derive both stamps from it, and in Accept treat the expiry instant itself as already expired.
Store one instant in the fake and add each step to it, read the given clock a single time when creating, and compare strictly before the expiry when accepting.

fund-csharp/21-testing-web-apps-seams-an.instructions:
**Skills:** fakes · unique constraints · copies, not references  
**Level:** ★★☆

**Interview prompt.** "Our signup tests use a plain dictionary as the user store. They are green, yet production answers 500 when `Ana@x.io` and then `ana@x.io` sign up. Write a fake the tests can trust."

**Why it matters.** A fake is only as good as the rules it keeps. The real store has a case-insensitive unique index on email and hands back a fresh row on every read; a fake that skips either rule lets tests pass for code that breaks in production.

**Your task.** Complete `InMemoryUserStore : IUserStore` in the types section:
- `User Add(string email, string name)`: give the new user the next id (1, 2, 3, ...) and store it. Emails are unique IGNORING CASE: a duplicate throws `DuplicateEmailException` (what the unique index does) and stores nothing.
- `User? Find(int id)`: a COPY of the stored user, or `null`. Changing the returned object must not change the store.
- `IReadOnlyList<User> All()`: copies of every user, in id order.

`Signup` (given) is the endpoint logic under test: 201 with the id, 409 on a duplicate email.

**Worked example.** `Add("Ana@x.io", "Ana")` returns id 1; `Add("ana@x.io", "Other")` throws and `All()` still holds one user.
hints: A fake earns trust by refusing what the real store refuses and by never sharing its own objects with callers.
Look for an existing user whose email matches ignoring case before storing anything, and build a new User object for every value you hand out, both from Find and from All.
Keep a private list of users, refuse an email that already exists in any letter case, number new users from one upward, and give callers fresh copies rather than the stored objects.
